Anjar at Kachchh dated 15.05.2009 rendered in Criminal Case No.927 of 1993, whereby the  learned trial Judge acquitted the original HC-NIC Page 1 of 5 Created On Tue Aug 15 12:24:50 IST 2017 R/CR.A/1760/2009 JUDGMENT accused, the opponents herein of the charges  for the offence punishable under Sections 7(1) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

2. The brief facts of the case of the prosecution, as set out before the learned  Trial Court, read as under:
3. The short facts giving rise to present appeal is that complainantFood Inspector, 
Shri R.V. Dodiya, BhujKutchh visited the firm of accused on 30/06/1992 at about 13:00 hours  in the presence of Panch and carried out the inspection.

The complainant orally informed the  accused that he wanted to analyze Besan before the Public Analyst and therefore to  purchase the same and issue Notice in the prescribed Form No.6 as per Rule 12. 
Thereafter, the complainant had purchased 450 Grams of Besan and paid the amount for that. 
The complainant has obtained the signature of the accused in a receipt regarding receiving  of amount.

Thereafter, the said sample of chili powder was stored in three airtight, 
cleaned and smell less bottles and sealed after following due procedure of law in the  HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Tue Aug 15 12:24:50 IST 2017 R/CR.A/1760/2009 JUDGMENT presence of the Panch witness.
The complainant also obtained signatures of panchas in the  panchnama he drew at the time of taking sample.
Thereafter, he sent the samples to the  Public Analyst, Rajkot for analysis.
The Public Analyst after analyzing the sample  opined as under: "The sample of Besan is adulterated as it does not comply with the standards  and provisions of PFA Act, 1954."

After the report of the Public Analyst, the complainant obtained the permission of  Local Health Authority and filed the complaint against the present accused in the Court of  l e a r n e d P r i n c i p a l S e n i o r C i v i l J u d g e & J M F C , 
Anjar at Kachchh being Criminal Case No.927 of 1993.

The learned Principal Civil Judge & 
JMFC, Anjar at Kutchh vide his judgment and order dated 15.05.2009 acquitted the  present respondentaccused person from the offences with which he was charged.

4. At the end of the Trial and after recording the statement of the accused under  Section 313 of Cr.P.C. and hearing the arguments on behalf of the prosecution and the  HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Tue Aug 15 12:24:50 IST 2017 R/CR.A/1760/2009 JUDGMENT defence, the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, AnjarKachchh acquitted  the accused of all the charges leveled against them.
On completion of the trial, the Sessions  Court passed the judgment and order acquitting the opponents.
5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the  learned Sessions Court, the appellantState has preferred the present Criminal Appeal.
6. Heard Ms. Reeta Chandarana, the learned APP for the State.
There is no representation  on behalf of the respondent.

sentences.text: 7. Ms. Chandarana, the learned APP submits that the learned Magistrate acquitted the  respondent on the ground of delay of one year and one month in lodging the complaint.
The  findings of the learned Magistrate that there are multiple violation for robbery provisions is not  correct in view of the detailed oral evidence of the complainant.

She, therefore, 
urges that the appeal may be allowed and the respondent may be convicted.
HC-NIC Page 4 of 5 Created On Tue Aug 15 12:24:50 IST 20  R/CR.A/1760/2009 JUDGMENT 8.
Having perused the impugned judgment and order as well as the oral and  documentary, obtainable on the record.

I am of the opinion, that though the delay of one  year and one month itself would not be supported the prosecution case to the  m a n d a t o r y p r o v i s i o n s w h i c h a r e i n f r i n g e d i n t h e p r e s e n t c a s e w h i l e  taking the sample of the food article as also the consent at Exhibit15.
Which is apparently suffers  from nonapplication of mind.
The learned trial Judge has recorded the findings  that there are multiple prejudice of mandatory provisions.

Upon reappreciation of the  evidence I am of the view that the findings recorded by the learned trial Judge do  not warrant interference in this acquittal appeal as they cannot be said to perverse or illegal.
9. For the foregoing reasons, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

10. Record and proceedings ordered to be remitted back to the trial Court forthwith. 
(A.G.URAIZEE,J) Manoj HC-NIC Page 5 of 5 Created On Tue Aug 15 12:24:50 IST 2017 State Of Gujarat vs Jitendrakumar Shantilal ... on 28 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86192340/
